business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Applicability depends on the nationality and residence of the investor and ultimate owners.
France-China Bilateral Investment Treaty signed in 1984 and in force, subject to its continuing applicability and treaty succession rules.
France-China Double Taxation Convention signed in 2013 and in force from 2015.
France has an extensive network of bilateral investment treaties and double taxation agreements; treaty entitlement must be confirmed against the investor's ownership chain and tax residence.

Relevant European Union trade instruments may apply, including the EU-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement and provisionally applied agreements such as CETA, subject to personal and territorial scope.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT rules are in the French Monetary and Financial Code, including Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, Article L.561-2-2 defining the beneficial owner, Articles L.561-5 and L.561-5-1 concerning customer identification and verification, Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-2 concerning enhanced measures, Article L.561-15 concerning suspicious transaction reporting, and Article L.561-46 concerning beneficial-owner information. Implementing provisions include Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Beneficial-owner filing requirements are also governed by Articles R.123-1 and following of the Commercial Code, Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020, Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020, and related implementing orders. Corporate registration and filing are processed through the national electronic formalities portal established under Law No. 2019-486 of 22 May 2019.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and throughout the relationship, screen the company, all direct and indirect owners, beneficial owners, directors, managers, authorized signatories, counterparties, banks, and major suppliers against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union sanctions lists, applicable French national sanctions, and OFAC lists where a United States nexus exists. Conduct PEP, family-member, and close-associate screening using reliable commercial and official sources. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, high-risk countries, opaque holding chains, nominee arrangements, unexplained wealth, adverse media, unusual payment flows, and sanctioned-sector exposure. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, document screening results, resolve false positives, prohibit transactions involving designated persons, and file a French TRACFIN suspicious transaction report where legally required. OFAC screening is not universally mandatory under French law but is required or commercially necessary where United States persons, United States financial institutions, United States-origin goods, or dollar-clearing exposure exists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; National Business Register data portal: https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL must have a distinctive denomination sociale that is not misleading, unlawful, contrary to public order, or confusingly similar to a protected corporate name, trade name, domain name, or trademark. French is not generally mandatory for the company name, and Latin-script foreign names are generally admissible. Local accents and French orthography may be used. A non-Latin or transliterated name should be checked for technical acceptance and commercial distinctiveness. The legal form must be stated in constitutional and registration documents as Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL, together with the share capital and registered-office information. Name clearance at the registry does not create trademark protection; searches should also cover INPI trademarks, EU trademarks, domain names, and commercial-name databases.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any wording implying authorization, public status, regulated financial status, or governmental affiliation without legal entitlement
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a statutory company-name reservation period of 30 days through the company registry. A name may be used only after incorporation and registration, and preliminary clearance is not a binding reservation. Conduct INPI, RNE, RCS, trademark, domain, and adverse-name searches before filing. If the filing is rejected or a deficiency notice is issued, obtain the written reason, correct the denomination or supporting evidence, and resubmit through the Guichet unique within the stated cure period. For a formal decision of the competent registry or administrative authority, use the available administrative or judicial remedy identified in the decision, generally including a prior administrative complaint where appropriate and an appeal before the competent commercial court or administrative court. A rejection should not be treated as final legal confirmation of third-party rights; separate trademark or unfair-competition exposure must be assessed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SARL must have a genuine registered office in France under Articles L.123-11 and following of the Commercial Code. Commercial domiciliation through an approved domiciliation company is generally permissible if the provider holds the required authorization and the written domiciliation agreement satisfies statutory requirements. A manager's personal residence may be used subject to applicable residential, lease, condominium, planning, and notification rules. A virtual office that supplies only mail forwarding without lawful domiciliation, access to corporate records, and reliable contact capability is insufficient. For trade-finance factoring, reverse factoring, escrow, and cross-border payment activity, a virtual office is commercially and prudentially high risk because the activity requires demonstrable management, compliance, accounting, transaction-monitoring, records, and operational capacity in France. The SARL form alone does not authorize factoring or payment services. Factoring generally requires operation through an authorized credit institution or an appropriately authorized société de financement under the Monetary and Financial Code; payment services and escrow structures may separately require payment-institution or credit-institution authorization. Prior ACPR and legal-perimeter analysis is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official French percentage is published. For an ordinary low-risk company, unannounced physical inspection risk is generally low. For a newly formed entity conducting regulated factoring, cross-border finance, escrow, or high-value payment activity, a practical risk estimate is approximately 15% to 30% during the first three years, increasing materially where the registered office is a mass domiciliation address, the company has limited personnel, licensing status is unclear, or AML risk indicators exist. This is an operational risk estimate, not a statutory probability or government statistic.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), L.210-1 to L.210-10 (formation of commercial companies), R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.511-1 and L.511-10 (ACPR authorization), L.311-1 4° (factoring as regulated bank operation), and L.313-23 et seq. (Dailly assignment of trade receivables)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed exclusively through the INPI one-stop shop (Guichet Unique des Formalités) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société (M0 declaration) together with the signed Statuts (Articles of Association) and ancillary exhibits, submitted to the RCS with resulting issuance of the Extrait Kbis
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for an SARL under the Commercial Code; the amount is fixed in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least one-fifth paid on incorporation (balance within five years); in-kind contributions are fully paid-up at subscription and verified by a statutory auditor. Given the regulated factoring activity, the ACPR/CRR minimum initial capital threshold (EUR 5,000,000 for credit institutions) must be met; all cash subscriptions must be held on a blocked escrow deposit account in a regulated French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital has been fully subscribed and, with respect to cash contributions, paid up to the statutory minimum; RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at [address], and the corporate purpose shall include factoring, receivables finance and trade supply-chain finance; RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Manager (gérant) for an indefinite term, with authority to conduct ordinary operations, open escrow and SWIFT-wire payment accounts, and execute financing agreements; RESOLVED, that the Manager shall prepare and submit the ACPR authorization application and adopt the AML-CFT internal control policies; and RESOLVED, that all publication, registration and post-incorporation formalities be completed by such Manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and statutory drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI corporate name and trademark database (data.inpi.fr); external French counsel or notary for drafting the Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the INPI/RCS records to confirm that the proposed corporate name is available and not infringing prior trademarks; prepare the definitive Statuts in French, specifying the SARL legal form, duration, registered office, exact corporate object covering factoring of trade receivables and cross-border reverse factoring, share capital, and powers of the gérant; where in-kind contributions are made, appoint a commissaire aux apports to certify the value; obtain the written acceptance of the proposed registered office owner.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts of the SARL
Copy of valid identity document of each associate and the appointed manager
Certificate of registered office occupancy (attestation de jouissance des locaux)
Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration draft
Valuation report for any in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals an identical or confusingly similar prior mark, promptly amend the corporate name and re-run the search; if UBO documentation is incomplete, supply additional identification and ownership-chain evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share capital subscription and escrow deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; a notary may alternatively receive the funds under Code de commerce Article L.223-7
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked deposit account (compte de dépôt de capital) in the name of the company-in-formation with a licensed French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts; transfer the full cash share capital subscribed; obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the receiving institution; ensure that all in-kind contributions are fully transferred and their value certified; document the allocation of each share part (part) among the associates.
required_dossiers: Share subscription forms signed by each associate
Certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Bank particulars and SWIFT/IBAN confirmation of the blocked account
Valuation report for in-kind contributions
List of subscribers with number of parts subscribed and amounts paid
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or Caisse des Dépôts refuses to open the blocked account, instruct a notary to receive the capital and issue an equivalent deposit certificate; ensure the certificate expressly identifies the company-in-formation and the date of deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory incorporation notice in a legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcement gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) of the department of the registered office, e.g., Les Echos or a departmental JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the avis de constitution containing the corporate form (SARL), company name, corporate object, registered office address, amount of share capital, duration, name of the manager, and RCS city of registration; deliver the notice to the chosen legal gazette and pay the publication fee; obtain the original issue or justificatif of insertion to attach to the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the avis de constitution
Payment confirmation for the gazette publication fee
Original signed Statuts for reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette requires corrections to the notice, file a corrected version and request a consolidated publication or an attestation referencing the original date; never proceed to RCS submission without the final justificatif.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the complete incorporation case with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitting the case to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and other public administrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the official one-stop-shop portal and select the SARL incorporation category; complete the M0 equivalent declaration (Déclaration de constitution); upload a certified copy of the Statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the justificatif of gazette publication, the registered office occupancy certificate, the UBO declaration, and identity documents; if filing through an intermediary, attach notarized powers of attorney; select the standard tax regime (corporate income tax) and the commercial registration category matching ISIC 6492; submit the dossier electronically and retain the acknowledgement of receipt.
required_dossiers: Déclaration de constitution (M0 form)
Certified copy of the Statuts
Attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the bank or Caisse des Dépôts
Justificatif of publication in the legal gazette
Proof of registered office occupancy and owner consent if applicable
Identity documents of associates and manager
UBO declaration (S-8 form)
Powers of attorney if signing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique returns a caducité notice, complete the missing fields or documents within 15 calendar days and resubmit; if the greffe raises a substantive objection, request review before the juge commis à la surveillance du registre under Article R.123-31 of the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, issuance of Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office department, with INSEE and URSSAF downstream notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the filing by the greffe, the company is entered in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, obtaining its SIREN, SIRET and French company identifiers; obtain the official Extrait Kbis which is the sole proof of the legal existence of the SARL; coordinate with URSSAF for social registration and the local corporate tax centre for taxation formalities.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgement of receipt and validation from the Guichet Unique
Extrait Kbis
INSEE SIREN/SIRET notification
URSSAF confirmation of employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis issuance is delayed, request a temporary attestation from the greffe to support banking and counterparty formalities; in case of registration refusal, file a motion before the judge supervising the RCS registry for an order directing registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: ACPR prudential authorization for factoring activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) within the Banque de France, with possible delegation to the European Central Bank under the Single Supervisory Mechanism if the institution is classified as significant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing factoring transactions, submit a complete authorization application under Article L.511-10 of the Code monétaire et financier; the file must include the programme of activity, five-year business plan, demonstration of the EUR 5,000,000 minimum initial capital, governance and fitness-and-propriety records of the manager and shareholders, internal controls, AML-CFT policies aligned with Directive (EU) 2015/849, outsourcing arrangements, and the specific procedures for escrow-account and Swift-wire payment rails; respond to ACPR information requests and pay the applicable supervisory contribution fees.
required_dossiers: ACPR authorization application form
Programme of activity and business plan
Certificate of paid-up capital and proof of capital adequacy
Organisational chart and internal governance rules
Fitness and propriety file for the manager and qualifying shareholders
AML-CFT internal policies and procedures
Detailed description of escrow and Swift-wire payment mechanisms
Outsourcing agreements and IT security measures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACPR requests additional information, respond within the prescribed deadline to preserve the application; if authorization is refused, file an appeal with the Administrative Court of Paris within two months or submit a revised application after curing the identified prudential or compliance deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for the financial operating license; Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) for occupational health and safety clearance; Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for environmental compliance of any auxiliary installations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'établissement de crédit spécialisé / société de financement specialising in factoring and trade receivables financing (Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.511-1, L.511-10 and L.311-1 4°)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité environnementale represented by the DREAL (Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal environmental impact assessment for pure office-based factoring activity; no installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) filing required unless auxiliary combustion equipment, such as backup electric generators, exceeds the registration thresholds listed under ICPE rubric 2910 (non-nuclear thermal installations above 1 MW); where such generators are installed, a prior registration declaration must be filed with the DREAL
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions are generated by the factoring operations; sanitary wastewater must comply with the local public sewerage regulations; office waste, e-waste and batteries must be separated and assigned to approved treatment and recycling channels under the AGEC Law; hydraulic and fuel-oil equipment, if any, must respect the ICPE discharge standards and storage requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the departmental fire and rescue service (SDIS) or the commission de sécurité for ERP-classified premises under Articles R.123-1 et seq. of the Construction and Housing Code; structural load inspection certificate for the registered office; electrical installation conformity certificate (Consuel) for new or modified electrical circuits; periodic workplace health and safety clearance by DREETS/CARSAT covering workstation ergonomics, emergency lighting and exits, first-aid equipment, fire drills, and the mandatory risk-assessment register (DUERP).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating through the enterprise tax portal impots.gouv.fr; VAT registration for non-established businesses is handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and the Direction des Non-Résidents for non-EU entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register economically in France: for an établissement stable or permanent physical presence, file at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce to obtain a SIREN and SIRET; then complete the enterprise tax registration process through the DGFiP to obtain a French VAT number. A non-EU entity without a fixed establishment must appoint an individual or legal entity authorized to act as its VAT representative (représentant fiscal) with DGFiP approval. EU-established entities may obtain direct VAT registration by filing Form 3551 (Cerfa 15717) or equivalent electronic filing. The VAT number is issued in the format FR + 11-digit SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). It may elect, for a maximum period of five fiscal years, to be taxed in the name of its partners under individual income tax (option for impôt sur le revenu) provided it meets the small-business conditions of Article 239 bis AA of the Code Général des Impôts. For VAT, entities can form a single taxable person (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C CGI, and corporate groups may elect fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI where the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general registration threshold for non-French suppliers making taxable supplies in France; any foreign supplier without EU establishment becomes liable to French VAT on the first taxable transaction. For EU distance sales of goods (B2C), the annual pan-EU distance threshold of EUR 10,000 applies (with the option to voluntarily register). For B2B supplies, the reverse-charge mechanism generally applies where the French customer is VAT-registered, but non-established sellers must register for French VAT when reverse charge is unavailable or for certain defined services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has implemented a phased mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting regime. All taxable persons established in France must be able to receive structured electronic invoices by 1 September 2026, and must issue e-invoices via a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the public portal Chorus Pro by the applicable phase (large enterprises by 1 September 2026; SMEs and micro-enterprises by 1 September 2027). Real-time clearance is achieved through XML invoice data transmission (Factur-X / UBL / CII), with mandatory digital reporting data fields, but no crypto-stamping or continuous real-time government pre-clearance is currently implemented in France.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 262 CGI, zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by or on behalf of the supplier to a destination outside the European Union, provided the exporter retains proof of physical exportation. Services supplied to non-EU customers, including factoring and receivables-financing transactions, are generally outside the scope of French VAT or exempt, not zero-rated under the export provisions. Financial and factoring transactions are standardly VAT-exempt under Article 261 C of the CGI and Article 135 of the EU VAT Directive, and therefore no French VAT is chargeable; such supplies are often subject to reverse charge or no VAT, but this is not technically an export zero-rating relief.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Déclaration Administrative Unique or Single Administrative Document)
Proof of export / dispatch from French customs territory (exit confirmation from the Customs Automated Clearance System)
Bill of Lading or airway bill (transport documentation confirming the goods have left the EU)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence confirming payment was received from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where a French exporter zero-rates supplies without valid documentary proof of export, the DGFiP may retroactively reclassify the supplies as taxable in France, reassess 20% VAT, and apply late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) of 0.2% per month. If a false declaration is made with bad faith or fraud, a fine of 40% of the tax at stake (or 80% for deliberate fraud) may be applied under Articles 1728, 1729 and 1731 of the CGI. Criminal penalties under Article 1741 CGI may also be assessed in severe cases. For factoring and supply-chain finance transactions, the DGFiP additionally scrutinizes whether the operation is a true assignment of receivables versus a disguised financing arrangement; if recharacterized as a loan, the VAT exemption remains but corporate tax and documentary withholding consequences may arise. Exporters must secure and retain all substantiating customs and banking documentation for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), the central bank of the French Republic and a member of the Eurosystem, acting in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty as the competent exchange-control and balance-of-payments statistics authority, and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the integrated licensing, AML/CFT and banking supervision authority for the French financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully liberalised and convertible foreign-exchange regime. As a Eurosystem member, the euro is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Capital Liberalisation Code; no French exchange-control authorisation, quantitative limitation, lock-up or prior licensing of outward transfers applies to transactions between residents and non-residents. The operative distinction is not convertibility but reporting and purpose-coding discipline: (i) current account transactions, including cross-border factoring settlements, trade disbursements, service fees and profit remittances, are unrestricted and require only correct classification for the mandatory cross-border transfer declaration; (ii) capital account operations, such as equity injection, shareholder loans and acquisition or disposal of participations, are equally free but require the bank to maintain documentation evidencing the economic substance of the flow; and (iii) any transfer of funds exceeding EUR 12,500 per calendar month to or from a non-EEA country must be declared to the Banque de France by the credit institution under Article R. 152-3 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier, CMF), using the DG Trésor purpose codes (motif de l'opération). Profit remittance hurdles for a French SARL are procedural rather than regulatory: distribution requires (a) audited or accountant-certified financial statements demonstrating distributable profits, (b) a shareholders' meeting distribution resolution, (c) satisfaction of the French 25% withholding tax for third-country parents subject to treaty reduction (e.g., 10% under the France-China treaty, 0% or 15% under other DTTs), with the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive eliminating withholding for EEA corporate parents, and (d) bank-level verification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain before release. The only material constraint for a factoring treasury is the statutory prohibition of financing a receivable in a manner equivalent to loan-back structuring and the requirement to maintain factoring collection accounts (comptes de recouvrement) separately from the operational account, as governed by the Dailly Law (articles L. 313-23 et seq. CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender regime exists in France. The former export domiciliation and mandatory repatriation system was abolished by the Loi de modernisation de l'économie (LME) of August 2008; exporters, factoring companies and trade financiers may therefore retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) at authorised banks, or convert to euro at freely negotiated market rates without any statutory ratio, and no time limit for repatriation applies. The only residual obligations are statistical: (i) the SARL's French credit institution must report each reportable cross-border settlement above EUR 12,500 to the Banque de France with the appropriate DG Trésor purpose code and, where available, the underlying commercial transaction reference; (ii) the SARL itself is subject to a direct balance-of-payments reporting duty if its aggregate cross-border transfers exceed EUR 750,000 per annum or if the Banque de France selects it for the quarterly trade-in-factoring survey; and (iii) for non-EEA export receivables purchased by the SARL, no proportion of proceeds must be converted to euro, but the entity must preserve the original invoice, the transport and delivery evidence, the assignment bordereau (bordereau de cession de créances professionnelles) and the notice to the account debtor so that the reporting bank can file a complete and compliant statistical record. These rules are consistent with EU Regulation No 2021/379 on balance-of-payments statistics, which leaves the eurozone without any capital-control restriction on export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_registration_mandate: Although France imposes no exchange-control permit for capital movements, a French SARL must complete the legal registration of any inbound equity injection: cash contributions must be deposited within eight days of subscription either with a bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and the depositary bank shall issue the mandatory bank certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds) without which the increase in capital cannot be registered with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. This certificate, together with the extraordinary general meeting resolution, the amendment of the articles of association, the appointment of the gérant and the updated UBO register (RBE), constitutes the documentary basis that the receiving bank attaches to the SWIFT MT103 or SEPA transfer file, thereby satisfying French AML and statistical reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fx_controls_on_non_eu_transfers: For all transfers between France and a non-EEA state exceeding EUR 12,500 per calendar month, the credit institution must file an electronic declaration with the Banque de France identifying the ordering customer, the beneficiary, the amount, the currency, the date and the DG Trésor purpose code. The purpose codes relevant to a factoring SARL include: capital participation for parent equity injections; loans for shareholder or intragroup advances; trade financing and receivables purchase for the underlying factoring settlements; interest, dividends and branch profits for profit remittances; and payment for financial services for factoring commissions. Erroneous or incomplete coding can trigger ACPR supervisory intervention, OFAC/EU-sanctions red flags and review by the French intelligence unit (Tracfin), so the treasury function must maintain a mapping table between each payment rail and the applicable purpose code.

Operational EUR Account, Factoring Collection Account (compte de recouvrement), FX Forward and Derivative Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is LOW for primary treasury, escrow and regulated collection rails, and MEDIUM for ancillary operating-treasury functions. Legal constraints are defined by the PSD2 regime transposed into the CMF (articles L. 521-1 to L. 525-15): a payment institution or electronic money institution (EMI) may not carry out factoring or any lending activity, because the purchase of trade receivables with financing features constitutes a credit operation reserved to ACPR-licensed credit institutions or sociétés de financement under article L. 511-1 and L. 313-1 CMF. Post-Brexit, UK-licensed EMIs such as Revolut and Wise no longer enjoy EU passporting and cannot open a core banking account for a French ACPR-supervised factoring entity unless they establish a French branch through the ACPR; French-regulated EMIs and payment institutions such as Qonto, Shine, Lemonway and Mangopay may lawfully host operating expenses, VAT flows and collections on behalf of the SARL, but they cannot serve as (i) the statutory capital escrow account, (ii) the factoring clients collection account where segregated funds of the SARL's clients are held, or (iii) the SWIFT-linked cash concentration account through which bank refinancing and client disbursements flow. The treasury blueprint should therefore use fintech EMIs only as a sub-ledger and payments-clearing aid for low-risk operating expenditure, while all regulated liquidity, factoring settlements and cross-border clearing must remain with full-service ACPR-regulated credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law (CMF articles L. 561-5 to L. 561-7; ACPR guidelines and position 2020-03) mandates full customer due diligence before account activation. For a corporate client with non-resident ownership and a financial-services licence, French banks require at least one physical interview at a French branch or, for the non-resident gérant, at a French consulate abroad for signature legalisation (légalisation de signature); the presence of the statutory manager holding signature power is the standard condition for the initial KYC interview. Remote video e-KYC is formally permitted by ACPR position 2020-03 but in practice is accepted only for ordinary commercial companies; for an ISIC 6492 trade-finance entity classified as a higher-risk sector, banks de facto impose an enhanced due diligence path: physical attendance of the gérant or of a mandataire with an irrevocable power of attorney (délégation de pouvoir notariée) for the first meeting, an on-site visit to the French registered office by the bank's compliance officer, and a second interview of the designated AML compliance officer of the SARL. The overall onboarding timeline is four to eight weeks, plus an additional two to three weeks where the UBO chain includes non-EEA jurisdictions. The Board of the SARL should prepare, before opening, the full corporate KYC kit: certificate of incorporation with SIREN, Kbis extract of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, articles of association, RBE registration proof, tax identification certificate, audited financial statements or opening balance sheet, the ACPR authorisation or registration proving the legal right to engage in factoring, the factoring operational procedure manual, sanctions-screening policy and the list of authorised signatories with specimen signatures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification: factoring and cross-border reverse factoring are treated as trade-finance activities with elevated money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk because the institution moves third-party funds across borders and may inadvertently fund sanctions-evasion schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ACPR licence or registration as a société de financement or credit institution; ASF (Association française des sociétés financières) membership certificate; the SARL's written AML/CFT programme under CMF articles L. 561-4-1 and L. 561-32, including risk assessment, internal controls, training records and the designation of the compliance officer (RCBE); detailed operating-model memorandum describing purchase of French SME receivables, Dailly bordereau procedures, debtor notification and the underlying trade documentation protocol (invoice, delivery note, transport document); EU and French sanctions-screening procedure implementing EU Regulations 269/2014 and 833/2014 and the Treasury list of the Direction Générale du Trésor; internal payment-flow mapping with segregation of collection and operational accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent or non-resident beneficial ownership: the parent and ultimate beneficial owners reside outside France or in a jurisdiction not perceived as a transparent financial centre, creating uncertainty about source of funds and economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully registered RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; complete UBO identification with passport or EU ID, proof of residence and source-of-wealth documentation for each person holding more than 25% of capital or control; notarised or consular-legalised powers; audited financial statements of the parent for the last two years; verified bank reference from the parent's home institution; French-domiciliation certificate and operating lease for the registered office; payroll evidence through DSN declarations of French-resident employees, evidencing that strategic treasury and compliance decisions are taken in France; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale of the cross-border ownership structure aligned with the factoring business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, high-concentration fund flows typical of factoring: frequent sweeps of collections from many account debtors into a single account, rapid outbound disbursements to cedant clients, and risk that pooled funds are used for loan-back or value-transfer arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved funds-flow mapping showing the separate collection account (compte de recouvrement), the operational account and the capital escrow account; contractual framework for each financing line: factoring agreement, reverse-factoring agreement and assignment bordereaux; monthly aged receivables report (rapport d'ancienneté) certified by an external expert-comptable or statutory auditor; debtor and counterparty concentration report per country and sector; sample underlying trade files with invoice, acceptance, customs and transport evidence for at least ten transactions; clear policy for non-performing invoices and litigation recovery procedure; and prohibition of re-advances against uncollected invoices unless supported by a new compliant Dailly bordereau.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels), management report and shareholders' approval minutes, filed at the Trade and Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry Clerk of the Commercial Court) via the guichet unique / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve fiscal-year accounts within six months of the financial year-end; the approved accounts must be deposited within one month after approval. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, approval must occur by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company to a court-ordered injunction with an astreinte (daily fine), civil damages, publication in the register delinquency list, and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation du RCS) after repeated defaults; managers may also incur criminal sanctions for obstructing the filing obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial annexes (liasse fiscale, declaration of results Form 2068-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) through the EDI-TVA / EFI electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, e-filing by the annual DGFiP deadline published each year, ordinarily in May of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year-end, the deadline is the second month following the close of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission attracts a late-filing penalty of 10% (5% if filed within 30 days) plus monthly late interest of 0.40%; if the tax authorities discover an undeclared taxable base, a 40% penalty plus interest applies, and the DGFiP may assess ex officio for complete failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration (CA12 annual return, or CA3 monthly/quarterly if the company opts for monthly payment) including VAT-exempt factoring commission income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the simplified actual VAT regime, annual CA12 return due by 30 April of the following year; for the normal monthly regime, CA3 returns are due by the 19th day of the following month. A final annual balancing return is due with the liasse if monthly payments were made.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment triggers automatic late-payment penalties of 5% plus 0.40% monthly interest; formal notice after filing default increases penalties to 10%; under-reporting or fraudulent concealment can raise the penalty to 40% or 80%, in addition to criminal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual prudential and financial reporting to the banking supervisory authority for the licensed factoring activity (COREP/FINREP simplified reporting and financial information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and Banque de France
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ACPR annual reporting schedule requires annual prudential reports and the certified annual accounts to be submitted within four months of the financial year-end (by 30 April for a calendar-year company), unless an extension is granted on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance can trigger ACPR disciplinary proceedings: warning, reprimand, supervision measures, fines up to EUR 5 million for legal persons under CMF Article L.612-39 in serious cases, and ultimately the suspension or withdrawal of the factoring/financial licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when it exceeds two of the three thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover EUR 8,000,000; average permanent employees exceeding 50. In addition, an ACPR-licensed factoring entity requires a mandatory annual statutory audit regardless of thresholds, and the ACPR may impose firm-specific audit or certification requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts of a French SARL must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) as codified in the Code de Commerce and ANC regulations. The EU-endorsed IFRS framework is permitted only for consolidated statements of groups and is not generally adopted as the local statutory framework for unlisted factoring entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO renewal form under French law, but the legal protocol requires the SARL to keep its declaration of beneficial owners (RBE) permanently up to date at the RCS. Any share transfer or other change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of the event. Before the annual shareholders' meeting approving the accounts, the share register and RBE are reviewed; a change is declared through the guichet unique, and if no change has occurred the directors re-validate the existing RBE record in the annual accounts filing package.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and decisions (Registre des procès-verbaux de gérance)
Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE)
Register of Pledges and Transfers of Parts (Registre des cessions et nantissements de parts sociales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 3,000 annual commercial domiciliation and registered-agent services in Paris/Île-de-France; USD 500 – 1,500 in provincial France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 – 30,000 annual fee for a licensed factoring SARL requiring a statutory audit and ACPR reporting; smaller, unlicensed SARL below thresholds may require no statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.00% standard rate; 15.00% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, ownership satisfying Article 219 CGI requirements).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for factoring activity. Applicable preferential mechanisms: reduced 15% corporate rate on first EUR 42,500 profit; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; French loss carry-back of one fiscal year with tax credit refundable over five years; IP Box preferential rate of effective 10% for qualifying patent licensing income; enhanced deduction for certain arm's-length trade finance costs under strict conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (Cerfa No. 11067) and the accompanying liasse fiscale (forms 2051 through 2058-SD, 2059-A-SD); mandatory electronic filing via EDI/EFI through an approved tele-transmission partner or the impots.gouv.fr secure portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (liasse fiscale); quarterly instalments (acomptes IS) for entities exceeding EUR 50,000 annual corporate tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year. For calendar-year entities closing on 31 December, the filing deadline is 3 May of the following year; if the deadline falls on a weekend or statutory holiday, it is extended to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN/SIRET, legal form (SARL), registered address, APE code (6492Z for factoring), French VAT number, and principal place of management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To be completed by the SARL's appointed French tax representative if the company is controlled from abroad; the representative must be authorized by the French tax authorities and be located in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box G / Box H (Net result before IS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before corporate income tax adjustments, determined under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-entity results are reported; non-resident shareholders must not consolidate their own income or losses in these boxes. Factoring fee income, discount income, and provisions for doubtful accounts are included according to French tax recognition rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of intercompany flows: management fees, factoring fees, reverse-factoring charges, interest, and any payments to non-resident related enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Arm's length pricing documentation must support every entry; if the SARL is engaged in cross-border factoring with related parties abroad, the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Article 57 CGI apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs: non-deductible provisions, excess interest, fines, gifts, depreciation above tax ceilings, and any profit distributions disguised as expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties must be carefully tested: excessive or undocumented royalty, interest, or factoring-fee payments will be added back unless the economic substance and actual benefit of the service are demonstrated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file after a formal notice: 10% penalty of the corrected corporate tax due, increased to 40% if filed more than 30 days after notice, and 80% in cases of fraudulent suppression; late-payment surcharge of 1% per month; statutory late-payment interest at 0.2% per month. For transfer-pricing documentation failures, an additional 5% penalty applies to the undocumented transaction amount with a minimum of EUR 10,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.00% domestic withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (Article 187-1 CGI), reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate parents under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) with a minimum 10% direct shareholding and a two-year holding condition; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 15% for direct direct investments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must submit to the French paying company a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, complete French Form 5000/5001, establish beneficial ownership, satisfy the applicable shareholding or ownership-test period under the treaty, and where payment was made at the statutory rate, file a refund claim with the French tax authorities within five years of the payment date. For dividends paid on or after 1 January 2020, reduced withholding is applied at source if the documentation package is received by the payer before the payment date; otherwise refund procedures are used.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding of 33.33% on patent and copyright licensing fees under Article 182 B CGI; reduced to 0% for associated EU companies under Directive 2003/49/EC (subject to holding and substance thresholds); treaty reductions typically 0% to 10% for patents and 5% to 10% for trademarks. Interest: no general statutory withholding on arm's-length debt interest paid to unrelated non-resident lenders; however, interest paid to residents of non-cooperative states (ETNC) is disallowed and subject to a 75% withholding under Article 187-2 CGI; interest in excess of arm's length paid to a shareholder may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend subject to the 25% withholding rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File obligations apply when the French entity or its consolidated group has gross annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets exceeding EUR 400,000,000; below this threshold, smaller entities must nevertheless file Form 2257 (annual intercompany transactions declaration) where related-party flows exceed EUR 1,000,000 or where the entity owns 5% or more of another taxable entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute of the type found in offshore jurisdictions, but economic substance is enforced through Article 57 CGI (arm's length and actual performance), OST (Office of Transfer Pricing) guidelines, ATAD anti-abuse rules as transposed into French law (e.g., Article 2034 CGI), and the principal purpose test in French tax treaties. A factoring SARL must maintain real operational substance in France, including staff, premises, management decisions, accounting records, and a commercial purpose for its factoring activities; an artificial letter-box factoring vehicle will be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, and subjected to 80% fraud penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission or concealment of factoring fee income or discount income, issuing false invoices or credit notes, or routing income through artificial offshore factoring vehicles to suppress the French taxable basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax penalty of 80% (40% in bad faith cases) plus late-payment interest; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years; for organized tax fraud, fine increased to EUR 3,000,000 and imprisonment up to seven years; confiscation of assets and publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (manager) may be criminally prosecuted as the principal actor; the corporate veil is pierced where the entity was used as a mere instrument to commit fraud (abus de biens sociaux); personal assets may be seized, travel bans imposed, and a 15-year disqualification from managing a business may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure or refusal to produce the Local File, Master File, or CbCR documentation after formal administrative request, or submitting intercompany factoring and financing transactions without proper comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of 5% of the amount of undocumented transactions, with a minimum of EUR 10,000 under Article 1735, 4° CGI; reassessment of the profits with default interest; an additional 40% bad-faith penalty may be imposed on the reassessed tax if the omission is deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No direct automatic imprisonment, but civil liability for faute de gestion may be invoked when the manager’s failure to maintain documentation causes recovery of the group’s tax liabilities to fail; administrative injunctions and restrictions on the manager’s business activities may be issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident beneficial owners while wilfully failing to deduct the statutory withholding tax, or routing payments through conduit jurisdictions to circumvent treaty limitations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full withheld amount plus late-payment interest and a 40% bad-faith penalty (80% if deliberate concealment is established); the unpaid withholding tax becomes a personal legal obligation of the responsible director where the enterprise lacks sufficient assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid withholding taxes under the regime of personal responsibility for failure to perform statutory collection duties; criminal characterization as tax fraud can lead to five years imprisonment, restitution orders, travel bans, and confiscation of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a trade-finance factoring business without the required ACPR authorization or license, failing to perform AML/KYC customer due diligence, neglecting beneficial-owner declarations, or omitting suspicious-transaction reporting to Tracfin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties for exercising banking or finance activities without the required license: imprisonment up to five years and fine up to EUR 7,500,000; ACPR sanctioning committee may impose administrative fines up to EUR 100 million or 10% of global turnover; withdrawal of any license in force.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face automatic disqualification from managing a regulated financial institution; personal criminal conviction for money laundering (up to 10 years imprisonment); seizure of personal assets; and in cross-border cases, travel bans and extradition requests may be used.
